• Belongs to the Betta splendens complex.
  • IUCN Red List: Data Deficient (not enough information, but most likely highly endangered in the wild).
  • Captive bred.
  • Maximum standard length about 2.8 cm; listed max size 5 cm (2 inches).
  • Breeding: bubble nester.

The rarest of all the splendens complex, found only in the Mekong River basin in Cambodia, from the locality of Stung Streng. This species was once thought to be extinct, but a recent re-emergence has been reported by a handful of breeders.

Native to the Mekong drainage in Cambodia, particularly Stung Treng's swampy streams and ponds with dense vegetation and low oxygen. Thrives in stagnant, slightly acidic (pH 5-7.5), warm (22-27°C) waters, using its labyrinth organ for air-breathing.

• TDS: 60 - 200 (kept in soft water with low TDS to match other wild bettas, but they are more tolerant of water conditions)
  • pH: 5.0-7.0
  • Temperature: 24-29°C (75-85°F); much better coloration at a warmer temperature above 26°C (78°F)
Carnivorous. Fed live blackworms, frozen bloodworms and pellets.
Males are very aggressive and should be kept alone or in tanks with non-male bettas. Can be kept in a planted community tank of multiple females if there is adequate space.

Males display a brown to black body with iridescent green-blue "snake-scale" patterns, particularly prominent on fins and operculum. Red patches may appear on fins. Females are browner with faint green hints and less vivid markings. The operculum is black with a prominent iridescent green-blue "snake-scale" pattern, more widespread and vivid in males than in females.

Body is compact and slender with a stout head, reaching a maximum standard length of about 2.8 cm. Smaller and more streamlined than many Betta splendens complex relatives. Tail shape is exclusively roundtail, with short, rounded caudal and anal fins. Features up to 9 rows of black transverse bars on the caudal fin and 5 rows of round black spots on the dorsal fin, giving a distinctive "spotted" appearance.
